content.text: {"headline":"Approve R2: targeted IVR messaging and callbacks with a wider break shift. It is the best available plan at 72.6% over 13:00-15:00 but still short of the 80% target.","why":"Payments handle time has nearly doubled (560 s against 299 s forecast at 12:00), while calls and staffing are on plan. The likely cause is slowness in the CardMax card tool after this morning's release (ticket INC-20261019-1835, P4, link not confirmed). Doing nothing is predicted to give 57.2% (payments 49.2%) with 12.7% abandons. R2 raises the window to 72.6% (payments 66.0%, general 80.2%) and cuts abandons to 6.5%. It also gives the best rest-of-day figure at 86.4%, for INR 1,143 with no policy violations. No plan reaches 80% for the window, so R2 was chosen as the strongest option.","trade_offs":["R1 costs only INR 168 and gives 70.1% (payments 64.0%, abandons 6.9%). R2 adds 2.5 points and protects the 15:00 hour for INR 975 more, mainly by cancelling payments coaching 15:30-16:15.","P3 costs the same INR 1,143 as R2 but delivers only 65.2%, so R2 is clearly better value at that spend.","Moving breaks shifts load later: general breaks are delayed too, but general stays healthy at 80.2%, so the other queue is not put at risk.","Payments customers still face 66.0% service level during the window. Callers with declined cards will hear a known-issue message and some will be offered callback or chat."],"watch":"Watch payments handle time and the CardMax ticket. If handle time keeps rising beyond 560 s, or the ticket is confirmed and not fixed by 15:00, the gap will last longer than planned and payments service will fall further. In that case, consider pushing to raise the ticket's priority and involving the duty manager."}
